chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUdays, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when the shadow on the wall was one cubit, performed the zuhr prayer, and when it was two cubits, performed the ʿasr prayer.
I said: Walls differ; some of them are short and some of them are tall.

He said: The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم at that time was the height of a man, and the one cubit and two cubits were only set so that there would not be any supererogatory prayer at the time of an obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الْفَيْءُ: the returning afternoon shadow used to determine prayer time
key_terms.ذِرَاعًا: one cubit, a measure used here for the beginning of zuhr timing
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْنِ: two cubits, a measure used here for the timing of ʿasr

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith define the time of zuhr and ʿasr prayer by the shadow of a wall?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the timing of zuhr and ʿasr prayer by reference to the measure of shadow on the wall during the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also clarifies that these measurements were used as practical indicators to distinguish the time of obligatory prayer from the time in which supererogatory prayer might otherwise be performed.
